reason: Paper is part of the printing process, and plant fiber mixed with water seems like a useful starting point.
expectation: I expect a pulp or paper material, though it may need further processing.

alternatives.reason: Charcoal and water may make ink, but I chose to start with paper.

effect: The fiber and water made paper pulp, so I can continue toward paper.
reason: Combining pulp with cloth seems like the next step in forming paper.
expectation: I expect a sheet of paper, though it might require another step.

alternatives.reason: I also considered starting the ink, but will finish the paper first.

effect: The pulp and cloth made paper, completing one likely printing material.
reason: Charcoal and water seem useful for making the ink needed for printing.
expectation: I expect ink or an intermediate ink mixture.

alternatives.reason: Carving planks may help build the press, but I want to prepare the ink first.

reason: Carving the planks seems like a useful step toward making a printing surface or press component.
expectation: I expect a carved wooden component, though I'm unsure whether it will be a printing block or part of the press.

alternatives.reason: Paper and planks might also contribute, but carving seems more directly related to printing.

effect: Carving the planks made a printing block, which can now be inked.
reaction: The printing block was one of the expected possibilities.
reason: Inking the block is a natural next step toward printing.
expectation: I expect an inked printing block, ready to transfer an impression to paper.

alternatives.reason: Paper and planks might help build the press, but I want to prepare the block first.

effect: The printing block is inked, but the press still needs to be built.
reason: Paper and planks are the remaining direct combination, so I'll try them before placing materials at the dock.
expectation: I expect a paper-related printing component, though I'm unsure how the planks will be used.

alternatives.reason: Placing planks at the dock might help build the press, but its purpose is unclear.

effect: The paper and planks made a lantern frame rather than an obvious press component, so I'll try a dock preparation.
reaction: The lantern frame was unexpected and its relevance is unclear.
reason: Planks may form part of the press, so I'll place them at the dock and see what becomes available.
expectation: I expect placing the planks to enable a construction step, though I don't know why it needs the dock.

reaction: The new option suggests a construction step, though the dock's role remains unclear.
reason: Iron and planks may form the printing press, and this is the only new construction option.
expectation: I expect a press or a structural component for one, though I'm unsure why it requires the dock.

effect: The iron and planks made the press and revealed the goal of printing a page.
reaction: The screw-and-plate explanation clarified how the press works.
reason: Placing the inked block at the press should prepare it to print.
expectation: I expect the block to be positioned at the press, allowing paper to be combined with it.

alternatives.reason: I could place the paper first, but either preparation seems plausible.

effect: Placing the inked block enabled the paper-and-block combination at the press.
reaction: The next step is clear and matches my expectation.
reason: Combine the paper with the inked block to print the page.
expectation: I expect a printed page to complete the goal.

effect: The paper and inked block produced printed pages, completing the chapter and showing how the press reproduces marks.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the prepared materials become repeated pages.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the printing press was most worthwhile: the screw-and-plate explanation made its operation clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the paper lantern frame felt like a detour from printing, with no clear relevance to the goal.

surprise.text: Paper and planks made a lantern frame rather than a press component.

arbitrary.text: Building the press at the dock felt arbitrary; its role was never explained.

continue.text: I would probably continue: assembling the press and seeing how it reproduces pages was engaging, despite the unclear dock and lantern detour.
